note: Public official releases, plus a few labeled DEMO rows. DEMO rows are synthetic. Do not treat them as real quotes.

statements.text: Signed AB 179, a housing budget trailer bill that modernizes California’s affordable housing finance system, citing a 59% increase in residential construction since 2019 and pairing the bill with the $11.25 billion Veterans and Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026.
statements.quote: Every Californian deserves a place to call home, and through this work, we’re turning that goal into reality.

statements.text: Signed legislation placing the Veterans and Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026 — an $11.25 billion bond — on the November ballot to accelerate construction, rehabilitation, and preservation of affordable housing and support homeownership programs.
statements.quote: In California, we don’t turn away from the needs of our people—we meet them head-on. With the signing of SB 417, we are giving voters the power to help shape the future of housing in our state.

statements.text: Issued an executive order to strengthen AI standards for state procurement, requiring companies seeking state contracts to demonstrate privacy, security, and civil-rights safeguards, and directing CDT to recommend watermarking for AI-generated images and manipulated video.
statements.quote: California leads in AI, and we’re going to use every tool we have to ensure companies protect people’s rights, not exploit them or put them in harm’s way.

statements.text: Announced a partnership with Anthropic to provide AI tools to state agencies, framed as a continuation of California’s 2023 generative-AI executive order and later procurement and watermarking rules.
Announced $44 million for 15 tribal stewardship, salmon recovery, and desert protection projects as part of the state’s 30x30 conservation goal.

Introduced the MORE WATER Act and GROW SMART Act to reauthorize Bureau of Reclamation recycling programs, fund canal restoration, and pilot agricultural water-saving projects. Cited a DWR estimate of a 6 million acre-foot annual drinking-water deficit by 2040.
statements.quote: After years of severe drought and mounting climate impacts, California needs bold solutions and sustained federal investment to confront water scarcity challenges in both cities and agricultural communities across the state.

statements.text: Announced the Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act, arguing AI data-center buildouts are driving grid upgrades whose costs should not be passed to residential ratepayers.
statements.quote: Artificial Intelligence is already deeply impacting our society, economy, and national security, and it is critical that we maintain our international leadership – however that growth cannot come at the cost of consumers or society.

statements.text: With Sen. John Curtis, introduced the CLEAR Act, requiring companies to disclose copyrighted works used to train generative AI models and creating a public Copyright Office database of those notices.
Announced more than $300 million in Measure ULA affordable-housing funding plus $14 million in emergency rental assistance for Angelenos affected by recent emergencies.
statements.quote: This historic investment will provide relief to renters impacted by last year’s fires and will increase LA’s affordable housing supply. I want every Angeleno to be able to afford to live in their neighborhood.

statements.text: Released a Climate Action Plan at the Donald C. Tillman Water Reclamation Plant, noting the plant is being expanded to purify 45 million gallons a day by 2027 and reduce reliance on imported water, including water that feeds Mono Lake.

Signed the Family Zoning Plan, a citywide rezoning package intended to meet state housing requirements while keeping local control over the map and protecting rent-controlled buildings and historic landmarks.
statements.quote: With the signing of the Family Zoning Plan, we are creating a generational roadmap for how our city builds housing—so the next generation of San Franciscans can build their lives here. And we will do it the San Francisco way.
statements.sourceLabel: Office of the Mayor, San Francisco

statements.text: Signed legislation creating a Downtown Revitalization District to finance conversion of vacant downtown offices into housing, continuing the Heart of the City / Family Zoning push.
statements.sourceLabel: Office of the Mayor, San Francisco

statements.text: DEMO: Would support statewide density near transit if paired with tenant protections and anti-displacement funding.
statements.quote: Build more homes next to the train — and keep the people who already live there from getting priced out.
statements.sourceLabel: DEMO / synthetic — not a real quote

statements.text: DEMO: Would oppose a specific upzoning bill that added density without tenant protections.
statements.quote: I will not vote for more luxury boxes on a corridor if the bill forgets the renters already there.
statements.sourceLabel: DEMO / synthetic — not a real quote

statements.text: DEMO: Would require AI lenders and insurers to show their models do not illegally discriminate, with a private right of action.
statements.sourceLabel: DEMO / synthetic — not a real quote
